# selfhost

> One ledger, one review list and one team config for every coding agent on a laptop. `selfhost init` sets it up in one command: hooks in Claude Code and Codex, a starter selfhost.toml in observe mode, the repository's context files offered for `.selfhost/context/`, and the last 30 days of local agent logs imported. Without a terminal it asks nothing; `--import-context` or `--no-import-context` answers its one question. Solo mode sends nothing anywhere.

## Install, for a coding agent

- Published package: `npx selfhostai@0.1.0 init`
- From source: `pnpm install && pnpm --filter @selfhost/cli build && node apps/cli/dist/main.js init`
- Preview first: `init --dry-run` prints every change and writes nothing. `--json` prints one `selfhost.init/v1` object.
- Join a team while installing: `init --team "selfhost join <server> <invite>"`. A refused invite exits 1 and changes no files.
- Start from a preset instead of the starter rules: `init --preset startup|strict|oss|irreversible`. Only when the person asks for one.
- Moving from Conductor: `selfhost migrate conductor --dry-run` shows how each repository's Conductor setup, run and archive scripts land in `[runtime]` of selfhost.toml; without `--dry-run` it writes them (Conductor's files are never changed). `--history <unpacked export>` also imports workspace history into the ledger.
- The MCP server for agents (team rules, budget left, pending review items, who else works on a file, past decisions, and asking a person or for a one-time exception): `selfhost mcp install` adds `selfhost mcp` to Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and Goose (`--agent` to choose, `--dry-run` to preview, `selfhost mcp uninstall` to remove). Solo it reads the local ledger; in a team it talks to the team server as the person.
- Only the guardrails (pre-tool hooks that block destructive and secret-leaking calls in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode; Goose has no hooks): `selfhost guard install`, then `selfhost guard status`. No account or server.

## What it changes

- A hook running `selfhost hook <agent>` in ~/.claude/settings.json and ~/.codex/config.toml (or ~/.codex/hooks.json), each file backed up first as `<file>.selfhost-backup-<UTC time>`.
- ~/.selfhost/: the ledger (data/), hook events waiting for import (spool/), the files init changed (init.json), the team membership (config.json, team mode only).
- selfhost.toml at the git repository root when there is none: 4 rules, all in observe mode, the guardrails in enforce and the package guard in observe. With `--preset`, that preset's rules; some are enforced. An existing selfhost.toml is never replaced.
- The hooks apply the built-in guardrails before each tool call: force pushes, git reset --hard, rm -rf outside the workspace and reads of .env and key files are blocked unless `[guardrails] mode` in selfhost.toml says observe or off.
- No shell profile, API key or sign-in.

## Undo

- `selfhost init --undo` restores each agent config file byte for byte from its backup, unless it was edited since. The ledger and selfhost.toml stay. A person runs it: it refuses inside a coding agent session, but needs no terminal, so a person's script can run it.

## Privacy

- Solo mode: nothing leaves the laptop and no network request is made, except by `selfhost integrations check`, which calls the tools named in `[integrations]` to test them, and by the package guard while `[packages] mode` is observe or enforce (the starter file and the presets turn it on in observe; it is off without a `[packages]` table), which looks each install up in its public registry.
- Agents do not approve: `selfhost inbox approve|deny`, `review approve|deny`, `decide`, `policy promote` and `team policy push` are blocked in the hooks and refused inside an agent session. Ask the person. The ledger keeps no prompt text; raw hook payloads wait in ~/.selfhost/spool (mode 0600) until the next import.
- Team mode: each `selfhost import` sends the ledger to the team's server.

## Team server

- `selfhost up --provider hetzner|digitalocean|aws|ssh` sets up the shared server (HTTPS, daily backups, optional GitHub or Google sign-in) and prints the `selfhost join` line. `--dry-run` prints the plan and the cloud-init user-data and creates nothing. It needs cloud credentials (HCLOUD_TOKEN, DIGITALOCEAN_TOKEN, the aws CLI) or `--host user@host`, so ask the person before running it without `--dry-run`: it creates billed servers.

- `selfhost up --gateway` also runs the AI gateway (Bifrost). `selfhost gateway connect claude-code|codex|opencode|goose` issues the person's virtual key and writes the settings that send that agent's API traffic through it into the agent's own config (backed up; `selfhost gateway disconnect` restores the files byte for byte); `--print` and `env` print them instead. The key's value is shown once. Cursor, Copilot and agents signed in with a subscription are left unchanged (`--api-billing` overrides the subscription check). `selfhost gateway` shows the team's hard limits and what is left. Connect and disconnect are a person's: they refuse inside a coding agent session, and the hooks block an agent that runs them.
